name: Gotthard
summary: The Gotthard xenon time projection chamber was an early high-pressure gas detector for xenon-136 double-beta decay in Switzerland. Its event imaging anticipated later gas-xenon tracking calorimeters.
detection_principle: An enriched xenon gas volume supplies both the isotope and ionization medium. Charge readout measures deposited energy and track topology, distinguishing candidate two-electron decays from gamma-induced backgrounds.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The historical xenon-TPC programme is documented by the 1989 apparatus thesis and a 2019 retrospective review, which discusses later search results published through 1998.

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: A detector thesis documented construction and performance of the Gotthard high-pressure xenon chamber.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
